_comment: Template only -- copy to C:\ProgramData\SortViewCollector\config\collector_config.json and fill in real values. Never commit a filled-in copy anywhere (Git, a support ticket, a screenshot) alongside a real API token -- the token itself never belongs in this file at all, see _comment_token below.
_comment_installation_id: installation_id is the Installation ID shown for this Collector in SortView Super Admin (collector_installations.id). Required for a new install; copy it from Super Admin, never invent it. 0 here is a placeholder and is rejected at load time. A config from an older Collector without this key still loads, but its heartbeats will not update the installation record.
_comment_run_audit_path: Optional, omitted here -- local, privacy-safe run-history JSONL (one line per invocation, 30-day retention, aggregate metadata only, no patron/item content). Defaults to <log_path's own directory>\runs.jsonl automatically, so an existing config predating this key needs no edit at all. Only set this explicitly to put the file somewhere else. See docs/collector-v1-admin-guide.md's 'Reading logs/status' section.
_comment_batching: Optional, shown here at their defaults -- omit entirely to use the same values. max_records_per_batch matches the value already proven in months of live production use.
_comment_token: SORTVIEW_API_TOKEN is READ FROM THE ENVIRONMENT ONLY -- it must never appear in this file. Set it as a Machine-scope environment variable via collector/deploy/install-collector.ps1's token step (or set-sortview-api-token.ps1, reused from the continuous-agent deployment tooling) before running the collector or its preflight check.
_comment_parser: The production Tech Logic parser (checkins/rejects/acs) is wired in via collector/parsers.py -- an ordinary run parses and uploads real data for those three sources. The collector still fails closed (exit code 2) as a safety net if 'sources' names anything outside those three (e.g. a typo) -- see docs/collector-v1-admin-guide.md.
